definition: A reward token gained by reaching certain Chakra milestones. Used to remove Corruption Marks or as indicated by the board.
The chaotic, shifting energy that surrounds the players. If you reach 6 Corruption Marks, the Veil has overtaken you and you lose.
Gradient spaces between Chakras on the Veil Progression Board. Players pass through these on the way to each Chakra milestone.
A core milestone space on the Veil Progression Board. Reaching a Chakra may grant rewards (Aether Tokens or Corruption removal). Players never fall below their highest Chakra reached.
The measure of how much the Aethereal Veil is consuming you. Each Corruption Mark brings you closer to defeat. Reaching 6 Corruption Marks ends your game.
A token placed on your Corruption Track when you lose a round or land in a Corruption Zone.
Dark spaces on the Veil Progression Board. Landing here adds 1 Corruption Mark. You remain in the Corruption Zone until you win a round.
The seventh and final Chakra milestone at the top of the Veil Progression Board. Reaching it wins the game.
The player (or AI in solo play) who deals the Table's hand each round. In multiplayer, one player acts as Dealer and resolves the Table hand.
The 22 special (trump) cards in a Tarot deck. Each carries a Roman numeral that can be used as its point value.
The 56 numbered suit cards in a Tarot deck (Wands, Cups, Swords, Pentacles). Point values match face value, with court cards worth 11–14.
Going over the 50-point threshold with your Spread total, resulting in an automatic loss for that round.
A scoring bonus applied when your 3-card Spread forms a qualifying pattern: Flush, Straight, Three of a Kind, Straight Flush, or Royal Flush. Only one bonus applies per round.
Your final 3-card hand: 2 face-up cards plus your hidden face-down card. Revealed during Reveal & Resolve.
The dealer's 3-card hand (1 face-up, 2 face-down) that all players must try to outscore without Overreaching.
